question.text: Investing in an illiquid emerging-market corporate bond that yields 200 bps above comparable developed-market bonds is an example of capturing:

explanation.text: The Logic: Illiquidity premium = compensation for holding hard-to-sell securities. Common in EM corporates, unlisted bonds, private credit. The Trap: Arbitrage is mis-stated — no true arbitrage if illiquid. Credit-spread and immunization are distinct. Cross-Exam Context: Unique to XXI-B and XIX-B AIF context. Manager's Pro-Tip: Illiquidity premium compensates only if you actually hold to maturity. Forced redemption during stress vaporises the premium.
